title: fix(browser): reject replaced native host files before pairing
body:
Related: #154370

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes native browser pairing accepting a manifest whose file is replaced after its ownership and mode checks but before its contents are read.

## User Impact

Native browser pairing and registration inspection validate the actual manifest and launcher bytes they consume. Existing owned private hardlinks remain supported, with the same real-user ownership and POSIX permission requirements.

## Why This Change Was Made

One private-file reader now uses the existing fs-safe descriptor admission path for both native-host pairing and registration inspection. This removes duplicate path-based checks while preserving the plugin's policy. It uses the existing released fs-safe dependency; no dependency change, migration, or operator action is required.

Existing installations remain compatible: registration JSON serialization, manifest fields and origin grammar, owned-launcher parsing, and immutable launcher construction/publication are unchanged. The change replaces admission/read sites and validation before cleanup; it preserves real-user ownership, private/executable modes, canonical paths, hardlinks, and separate Windows routing. No stored-format, schema, configuration, or protocol change is introduced.

## Evidence

- The manifest-substitution regression failed before the fix and passes with the shared reader; invalid artifacts are rejected before pairing is built.
- Seven focused browser suites cover pairing, registration, hardlink acceptance, and rejected file modes: 162 tests passed with `--maxWorkers=1` in 16.62 seconds wall time. The changed test file passed all 60 cases in 22.77 seconds wall time, including worker preparation.
- Existing upgrade and repair coverage passed, including the deployed fixed-launcher fixture, saved configuration, and retaining the previous registration when replacement publication fails.
- The actual launcher and CLI end-to-end suite passed all 8 cases, preserving a saved custom context and rejecting malformed or unauthorized requests before configuration or key work. Test execution took 5.270 seconds; the full 598.66-second command included a runtime rebuild and artifact coordination.
- `check:changed` passed all selected formatting, typechecking, lint, and guard checks; `git diff --check` passed. Independent scoped review found no actionable issues.
- Local proof ran on macOS. Existing Windows routing tests passed, but no new Windows live run was performed.
- Initial hosted CI failed in unchanged launcher tests because `fixtureRoots` was undefined. The branch was refreshed onto the canonical repair in #155825 with all four authored files byte-for-byte unchanged; fresh CI validates the repaired base.
- [Linux CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35756427658/job/106843672708) passed all 60 native-host cases (0.116 seconds summed reported test time; 166.48 seconds for the containing test shard).
